title: Onslaught
review: Very entertaining and crazy. It knows you want to see cool and sick shit, and it doesn't care about trying to be serious or suave like certain other highly competent assassin fantasies. More of the same subtle comedy as {The Guest}, this time more absurd and playful. Clearly a higher budget, but not breaking the bank. I like how these movies aren't grim or harrowing in any way. They have an air of {Mandy} or some other gritty revenge movies, but we don't really see anyone suffer. It's just normal life, transitioning to crazy chaos, without any kind of unpleasant trauma for revenge motivation. I knew this wasn't going to be an explicit sequel to {The Guest}, but they give you so few details about the world these films exist in, that you probably need to see them in order to avoid feeling completely lost. You don't get a Sense of how competent the brainwashed super soldiers are here, and the story hits harder if you assume they will be like David. Once again there's an 80s synth soundtrack to help make it feel like a modern take on the low budget action movies from that era. I think I liked this one a little less, only because there were too many characters in too short a runtime, and we didn't really get to know any of them.
